title: Bipolar I Disorder - Manic Episode Criteria
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Criteria

CORE ALIASES: Mania, manic episode, Bipolar I with manic episode.

DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA:
A. A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and abnormally and persistently increased activity or energy, lasting at least 1 week and present most of the day, nearly every day (or any duration if hospitalization is necessary).
B. During the period, three (or more) of the following (four if mood only irritable):
1. Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity
2. Decreased need for sleep
3. More talkative or pressure to keep talking
4. Flight of ideas or racing thoughts
5. Distractibility
6. Increase in goal-directed activity or psychomotor agitation
7. Excessive involvement in risky activities (spending, sex, business, driving)
C. The mood disturbance causes marked impairment or hospitalization or psychotic features.
D. Not attributable to substance or medical condition.

REQUIRED FEATURES: Full mania (not hypomania) + marked impairment or psychosis or hospitalization. History of major depressive episodes common but not required for Bipolar I diagnosis.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS: Bipolar II (only hypomania, no full mania), Cyclothymic (chronic subthreshold), Schizoaffective (psychosis outside mood episodes), Substance-induced mania, Medical (hyperthyroidism, steroids).

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: "No history of full mania", "only hypomanic periods", "symptoms only when using stimulants".

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR. CANMAT/ISBD guidelines emphasize mood stabilizer first-line.
